1. Import the data at https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/ds_salaries.csv

    The data description can be found at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/saurabhshahane/data-science-jobs-salaries
    
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
df <- read_csv("https://bryantstats.github.io/math421/data/ds_salaries.csv")
str(df)
```
   

2. Is there any column that contains NAs?

```{r}
colSums(is.na(df))
```
**There are no columns that contain NAs.**

3. What is the most frequent job title in the data?

```{r}
df |> count(job_title) |> arrange(-n)
```

**"Data Scientist" is the most frequent job title in the data.**

4. Find the average salary data of the three most frequent job titles in the data. 

```{r}
df |> 
  filter(job_title %in% c("Data Scientist", "Data Engineer", "Data Analyst")) |> 
  group_by(job_title) |> 
  summarise(mean_salary = mean(salary_in_usd))
```


5. What is the job title that have the highest average salary?

```{r}
df |> 
  group_by(job_title) |> 
  summarise(mean_salary = mean(salary_in_usd)) |> 
  arrange(-mean_salary)
```

**"Data Analytics Lead" has the highest average salary.**

6. Which country gives the highest salary on average?

```{r}
df |> 
  group_by(company_location) |> 
  summarise(mean_salary = mean(salary_in_usd)) |> 
  arrange(-mean_salary)
```

**Russia gives the highest average salary.**

7. Plot five meaningful plots. All plots should have title, caption, and appropriate labels.

```{r}
# 1
df |> 
  group_by(work_year) |> 
  summarise(avg = mean(salary_in_usd)) |> 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_line(mapping = aes(x = work_year, y = avg)) +
  labs(x = 'Year',
       y = 'Salary (in USD)',
       title = 'Average Salary by Year',
       caption = 'The average salary of data science jobs increases over time, with a large increase from 2021 to 2022.')
```


```{r}
# 2
df |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = experience_level, y = salary_in_usd, fill = experience_level)) +
  labs(x = 'Experience Level',
       y = 'Salary (USD)',
       fill = 'Experience Level',
       title = 'Salary Distribution by Experience Level',
       caption = 'Entry-level and mid-level jobs have a small difference between their median salaries.')
```


```{r}
# 3
df |> 
  group_by(experience_level, work_year) |> 
  summarise(avg = mean(salary_in_usd)) |> 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_line(mapping = aes(x = work_year, y = avg, color = experience_level)) +
  labs(x = 'Year',
       y = 'Salary (in USD)',
       color = 'Experience Level',
       title = 'Average Salary by Experience Level by Year',
       caption = 'All experience levels, except executives, did not see a significant change in average salary over time.')
```


```{r}
# 4
df |> 
  mutate(remote_ratio = as.character(remote_ratio)) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(mapping = aes(x = employment_type, fill = remote_ratio), position = 'fill') +
  labs(x = 'Employment Type',
       y = 'Proportion',
       fill = 'Remote Ratio',
       title = 'Remote Work Distribution by Employment Type',
       caption = 'Contract workers are fully remote, and no employment type is in office 100% of the time.') 
```


```{r}
# 5
df |> 
  mutate(remote_ratio = as.character(remote_ratio)) |> 
  group_by(remote_ratio, work_year) |> 
  summarise(avg = mean(salary_in_usd)) |> 
  ggplot() + 
  geom_line(mapping = aes(x = work_year, y = avg, color = remote_ratio)) +
  labs(x = 'Year',
       y = 'Salary (in USD)',
       color = 'Remote Ratio',
       title = 'Average Salary by Remote Ratio by Year',
       caption = 'Fully remote workers tend to have the highest average salaries.')
```
